thinkingCanDisable.note: The API accepts disabled at effort high or below and returns 400 at xhigh or max. Claude Code offers no off switch for this model, so a Claude Code route cannot disable thinking.

guidance.text: Anthropic positions it for high-volume, latency-sensitive work such as classification, extraction, routing and subagent tasks, with the lowest latency and price in the current lineup.
guidance.locator: Compare models table, Description, Comparative latency and Pricing rows

guidance.text: In Claude Code the haiku alias reaches Haiku 5.5 on the Anthropic API from v2.1.293; on Platform on AWS, Bedrock, Agent Platform and Foundry it still reaches Haiku 4.5. Pin claude-haiku-5-5 by name.
guidance.locator: Model aliases, provider table; Version history

guidance.text: Effort defaults to medium; start there, including for agentic coding. Use low for chat and simple volume work. xhigh and max need measured gains over Sonnet 5.5. It is the first Haiku with effort levels.
Thinking is on by default. disabled is accepted at high effort or below and returns 400 at xhigh or max; budget_tokens always returns 400. To think less, lower effort first.
Claude Code shows no off switch for thinking on Haiku 5.5, and MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0 has no effect there. Use a lower effort level to reduce thinking in a Claude Code route.
guidance.locator: Extended thinking, paragraph after the controls table

guidance.text: Thinking counts toward max_tokens, which can reach 128000, so limits sized for Haiku 4.5 can stop after a thinking block. The newer tokenizer also yields about 30 percent more tokens for the same text.
guidance.locator: Behavior changes, Same text counts as more tokens; New capabilities, Larger context window and output

guidance.text: In long agent prompts at low effort it can stop early or report a change done without running a check. Raise effort, or ask for a real test, type-check or build run before it reports done.
guidance.locator: Prevent early stopping in long agent prompts; Tell coding agents to verify their changes

guidance.text: With a search tool, give it today's date. At low effort or with long system prompts also say its training data is old so changed facts need a search. A blanket always-search rule adds searches without better answers.

With thinking off and a JSON output format it may skip a tool call it needs. Keep adaptive thinking on, drop the output format on turns that need a tool, or force the call; it still accepts forced tool_choice.
guidance.locator: Use adaptive thinking with JSON output and your own tools

guidance.text: Assistant prefill returns 400 even with thinking off, so end messages with a user turn. Omit temperature, top_p and top_k. Computer use on the API and Google Cloud needs the computer_toolset_20260801 toolset.
guidance.locator: Summary of changes from Claude Haiku 4.5

guidance.text: Keep user text out of tool_result blocks. Send mid-turn user input as a user turn after the last tool result, with harness notices in a separate system message, or it may treat the text as injected and ignore it.
With thinking off or at low effort it sometimes writes reasoning-like text into the reply that users see. If you see it, switch to adaptive thinking at medium effort.
guidance.locator: Keep reasoning out of user-facing text

guidance.text: Safety classifiers can decline cyber, frontier_llm, bio and general_harms requests with stop reason refusal. There is no server-side fallback, so handle the refusal in the client; resending usually repeats it.

Claude Code's automatic fallback covers flagged requests from Fable, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5 only, and does not name Haiku 5.5. Do not expect it to re-run a refused Haiku 5.5 request on another model.

Thinking blocks work only in the account that produced them and only while the system prompt, tools and earlier turns are unchanged. Editing history can fail a replayed block with a 400, so keep it append-only.
guidance.locator: Replay thinking blocks through the account that produced them; Keep earlier turns unchanged

guidance.text: Priority Tier is not supported on Haiku 5.5, so capacity committed on Haiku 4.5 does not carry over and must be planned separately.
